claims.statement: Addr v2 supports longer endpoint addresses, including new-generation Onion and I2P addresses, that do not fit the legacy 128-bit field.

evidence.quote: This document proposes a new P2P message to gossip longer node addresses over the P2P network. This is required to support new-generation Onion addresses, I2P, and potentially other networks that have longer endpoint addresses than fit in the 128 bits of the current addr message.

claims.statement: An addrv2 entry has time, CompactSize services, network ID, variable-length address and port, replacing the fixed 16-byte IP field.

evidence.quote: Its format is similar to the current addr message format, with the difference that the fixed 16-byte IP address is replaced by a network ID and a variable-length address, and the services format has been changed to [https://en.bitcoin.it/wiki/Protocol_documentation#Variable_length_integer CompactSize].

claims.statement: The addrv2 entries are synthetic single-entry teaching packets, not real endpoints or a live address book.

evidence.quote: Its format is similar to the current addr message format, with the difference that the fixed 16-byte IP address is replaced by a network ID and a variable-length address

claims.statement: One addrv2 message can contain up to 1,000 addresses and clients should reject more.

evidence.quote: One message can contain up to 1,000 addresses. Clients SHOULD reject messages with more addresses.

claims.statement: An addrv2 address has a maximum length of 512 bytes and longer addresses should be rejected.

evidence.quote: Field addr has a variable length, with a maximum of 512 bytes (4096 bits). Clients SHOULD reject messages with longer addresses, irrespective of the network ID.

claims.statement: The addrv2 services field uses CompactSize rather than a fixed eight-byte encoding.

evidence.quote: the services format has been changed to [https://en.bitcoin.it/wiki/Protocol_documentation#Variable_length_integer CompactSize].
Service bits. A bit field that is 64 bits wide, encoded in [https://en.bitcoin.it/wiki/Protocol_documentation#Variable_length_integer CompactSize].

claims.statement: The teaching model checks encoding, truncation, trailing data, size and selected range rules, and never performs address-book validation or network contact.

evidence.quote: Clients SHOULD reject messages that contain addresses that have a different length than specified in this table for a specific network ID, as these are meaningless.

claims.statement: BIP 155 reserves IPv4, IPv6, Tor v2, Tor v3, I2P, CJDNS and Yggdrasil with exact address lengths.

evidence.quote: | 0x01 | IPV4 | 4
| 0x02 | IPV6 | 16
| 0x03 | TORV2 | 10
| 0x04 | TORV3 | 32
| 0x05 | I2P | 32
| 0x06 | CJDNS | 16
| 0x07 | YGGDRASIL | 16

claims.statement: Clients should reject addresses whose length differs from the length reserved for their network ID.

evidence.quote: Clients SHOULD reject messages that contain addresses that have a different length than specified in this table for a specific network ID, as these are meaningless.

claims.statement: Clients should not gossip addresses from unknown networks because they cannot validate them; future IDs must be reserved in a new BIP.

evidence.quote:
Clients SHOULD NOT gossip addresses from unknown networks because they have no means to validate those addresses and so can be tricked to gossip invalid addresses.

Further network ID numbers MUST be reserved in a new BIP document.

claims.statement: Tor v2 is no longer operational; clients must not gossip or relay it and must ignore it on receive.

evidence.quote: Tor v2 is no longer operational; clients MUST NOT gossip or relay Tor v2 addresses and MUST ignore them on receive

claims.statement: Tor v3 uses the 32-byte public key in the address field, which is enough to reconstruct the onion address.

evidence.quote: Tor v3 addresses MUST be sent with the TORV3 network ID, with the 32-byte PUBKEY part in the address field. As VERSION will always be '\x03' in the case of v3 addresses, this is enough to reconstruct the onion address.

claims.statement: IPv4-in-IPv6 and OnionCat embedded addresses must not be treated as ordinary IPv6; canonical network IDs avoid duplicate peer identities.

evidence.quote: Such addresses already have a canonical encoding under their own network ID and MUST NOT be sent with the IPV6 network ID. Clients SHOULD ignore IPV6 addresses that fall into these reserved ranges on receive, since the same address received under two network IDs would otherwise be treated as two distinct peers.
Clients SHOULD ignore OnionCat (fd87:d87e:eb43::/48) addresses on receive if they come with the IPV6 network ID.

claims.statement: sendaddrv2 must only be sent in response to version and before verack, and does not state a preference about unrequested address messages.

evidence.quote: Introduce a new message type sendaddrv2. Sending such a message indicates that a node can understand and prefers to receive addrv2 messages instead of addr messages. I.e. "Send me addrv2". Sending or not sending this message does not imply any preference with respect to receiving unrequested address messages. The sendaddrv2 message MUST only be sent in response to the version message from a peer and prior to sending the verack message.

claims.statement: Peers that did not emit sendaddrv2 keep receiving legacy addr messages without the new address types.

evidence.quote: For older peers, that did not emit sendaddrv2, keep sending the legacy addr message, ignoring addresses with the newly introduced address types.

claims.statement: Clients are recommended to gossip addresses from all known networks, even when not connected to them, which can help multi-homed nodes and obscure which networks a node uses.

evidence.quote: Clients are RECOMMENDED to gossip addresses from all known networks even if they are currently not connected to some of them. That could help multi-homed nodes and make it more difficult for an observer to tell which networks a node is connected to.

claims.statement: I2P uses the decoded 32-byte SHA-256 hash as the address field.

evidence.quote: I2P uses 52 characters (256 bits) to represent the full SHA-256 hash, followed by .b32.i2p. I2P addresses MUST be sent with the I2P network ID, with the decoded SHA-256 hash as address field.

claims.statement: CJDNS addresses are IPv6 addresses in fc00::/8.

evidence.quote: Cjdns addresses are simply IPv6 addresses in the fc00::/8 range

claims.statement: Yggdrasil addresses are IPv6 addresses in 0200::/7.

evidence.quote: Yggdrasil addresses are simply IPv6 addresses in the 0200::/7 range

claims.statement: Decoding an addrv2 endpoint does not establish its existence, reachability, ownership or safety.

evidence.quote: Clients SHOULD NOT gossip addresses from unknown networks because they have no means to validate those addresses and so can be tricked to gossip invalid addresses.
